utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, have the accused brought in and call the case. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is the case IT-95-9-PT, the Prosecutor versus Stevan Todorovic, also known as Stiv, also known as Stevo, also known as Monstrum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, you may be seated. Can we have the appearances, the Prosecution first, as soon as the photographer has finished. Madam Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, as you know, my name is Nancy Paterson. I'm representing the Office of the Prosecutor today. To my right is the new senior trial attorney assigned to this case, Mrs. Anne Haslund from Denmark. Since she has just recently arrived at the Tribunal, I will be handling the session today, but at future sessions, Mrs. Haslund will be the lead attorney. On her right is John Michelich.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First of all, we wish Ms. Anne Haslund welcome. Am I pronouncing your name correctly, Haslund? Is that your name, Madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASLUND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: On behalf of my colleagues, we wish you welcome to the Office of the Prosecutor and, for the moment, to this Chamber. The Defence counsel for Mr. Todorovic is?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Goran Neskovic, attorney at law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I should like to recall that on the 30th of September, we asked Mr. Todorovic, who had just been arrested, to indicate, with the help of his counsel, how he pleaded, whether he pleaded guilty or not guilty. As you recall, Mr. Neskovic, your client, said that the conditions of his arrest and the medical consequences of that arrest, that is, the blow that he suffered on his head, caused him to suffer, and that due to that injury, he didn't consider himself capable of pleading. You asked the Chamber to undertake additional medical examinations, more specifically, to be examined by a scanner. Dr. Mosmans, who is a neurologic specialist, gave us his report on the 8th of October and said that there was no irregularity in the condition and that he didn't consider any scanning examination necessary, as his neurological examination showed that there were no abnormalities. The accused was informed of this, as well as both parties. Under those conditions, I turn now to Mr. Todorovic. Mr. Todorovic, will you please rise? My first question is, how do you feel, Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Mr. President, I feel much better now, and I would like to thank you personally and the Chamber in general for providing this opportunity to me and for the high regard that you showed in respect of me and my health. I hope that I will not suffer any additional consequences. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. That was quite normal, because you told us that you were in pain. When listening to the indictment, it was important to make sure that you could understand well what the Prosecution is charging you with before pleading. You also remember, Mr. Todorovic, and you will tell me if you do, that the indictment was read to you. Do you wish us to reread it or to simply remind you of the counts? I'm asking your opinion, and I will ask your Defence counsel for his opinion too. Would you like us to read the whole indictment and ask you to plead on each count, or if you prefer another procedure. What is your feeling? Would you like your Defence counsel to express his opinion instead of you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Mr. President, my counsel, Mr. Neskovic, read to me the indictment in its entirety at the detention unit, and I do understand it. As far as I'm concerned, there is no need for a full reading of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I now turn to Mr. Neskovic. Do you agree with the position taken by your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Mr. President. Only a reading of the individual counts is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Madam Nancy Paterson, are you in agreement with this procedure, bearing in mind what happened at the previous initial appearance?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have no objections to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I turn to the registrar now, and in full agreement with the accused, this will enter in the record. We are going to ask Mr. Dubuisson to read, with precision, the counts that concern Mr. Todorovic in the present indictment. We are going to ask Mr. Todorovic whether he pleads guilty or not guilty. Mr. Dubuisson, let us take the indictment. Counts 27, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will begin with paragraph 28. You will read the paragraph, the title of the count, and then read each of the counts. After each count, Mr. Todorovic, I will ask you to tell the Judges whether you plead guilty or not guilty. Mr. Dubuisson, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Counts 27 to 29, killing of Anto Brandic: 28) On about 29 July, 1992 in the hallway of the SUP building in Bosanski Samac, Stevan Todorovic and others killed Anto Brandic, also known as Antesa, by repeatedly beating and kicking him with police batons and heavy boots. By these actions, Stevan Todorovic committed or otherwise aided and abetted: Count 27: a grave breach recognised by Article 2(a) (wilful killing) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, regarding Count 27, in agreement with your counsel, do you intend to plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty in respect of this count.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 28, Mr. Dubuisson.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 28: a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute and Article 3(1)(a) (murder) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 28, do you plead guilty or not guilty, Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 29: a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(a) (murder) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Dubuisson, let us go on to Counts 30 to 32; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Counts 30 to 32, beatings in the SUP building: 29) On about 29 July, 1992 in the hallway of the SUP building in Bosanski Samac, Stevan Todorovic and others repeatedly beat and kicked Enver Ibralic, Hasan Jasarevic, Omer Nalic, and Father Jozo Puskaric with police batons and heavy boots, thereby causing the victims physical injury. By these actions, Stevan Todorovic committed or otherwise aided and abetted: Count 30: a grave breach (wilfully causing great suffering) recognised by Article 2(c) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Count 31.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 31: a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute and Article 3(1)(a) (cruel treatment) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 32: a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(i) (inhumane acts) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Counts 33 to 35, beating of Silvestar Antunovic. 30) On about 15 July, 1992 in the gymnasium of the Bosanski Samac primary school, Stevan Todorovic and others repeatedly beat Silvestar Antunovic with a large wooden club. As a result of the beating, Silvestar Antunovic suffered partial paralysis and other serious physical injury. By these actions, Stevan Todorovic committed or otherwise aided and abetted: Count 33: a grave breach recognised by Article 2(c) (wilfully causing great suffering) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 34: a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute and Article 3(1)(a) (cruel treatment) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 35: a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(i) (inhumane acts) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Counts 36 to 38, sexual assault. 31) On about 13 June, 1992 in the hallway of the Bosanski Samac SUP building, Stevan Todorovic forced Witness A and Witness B to perform sexual acts upon each other in the presence of several other prisoners and guards. By these actions, Stevan Todorovic instigated, ordered, and committed: Count 36: a grave breach recognised by Article 2(b) (inhumane treatment) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 37: a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute and Article 3(1)(c) (humiliating and degrading treatment) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 38: a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(g) (rape, which includes other forms of sexual assault) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Counts 39 to 41, torture of Omer Nalic. 32) On about 19 June, 1992 at the Bosanski Samac primary school, while questioning Omer Nalic about a radio transmitter, Stevan Todorovic ordered three men to beat Omer Nalic. By these actions, Stevan Todorovic instigated, ordered, committed, or aided and abetted: Count 39: a grave breach recognised by Article 2(b) (torture) of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 40: a violation of the laws or customs of war recognised by Article 3 of the Tribunal Statute and Article 3(1)(a) (torture) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 41: a crime against humanity recognised by Article 5(f) (torture) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may be seated, Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Todorovic, the written record of this hearing has registered the fact that you have pleaded not guilty to all the counts alleged by the Office of the Prosecutor. I turn to Mrs. Nancy Paterson to ask her how she foresees the procedural proceedings before this Tribunal, where we are regarding the disclosure of statements of the accused and other persons in support of the indictment. I will also ask the opinion of the Defence, whether we can set at least a provisional timetable. Mrs. Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think the office of the Prosecutor has been proceeding with the discovery obligations in a very timely matter. We have provided all the material in support of this indictment to Mr. Neskovic at the last appearance on the 30th of September, 1998. We have complied with Rule 66(a)(i). All material has been turned over, and that's been turned over in the language that Mr. Todorovic can understand. We are prepared to turn over some additional discovery material to Mr. Neskovic that we have already provided to the other three Defence attorneys for the other three accused. We can turn that over almost immediately, if the Court so prefers. I believe that we did mention at the last proceeding that, as a result of the arrival of Mr. Todorovic, we do anticipate amending this indictment to reflect his inclusion with the other three men that we have in custody. We are prepared to proceed with submitting that amended indictment as quickly as possible, pending some discussions we would like to have with Mr. Neskovic before we make that final decision. We have been proceeding with the discovery for the other three accused in a very timely manner. We have turned over all of the witness statements that we're obligated to up to this point in time. We have complied with their request under Rule 66. We will be providing a significant amount of additional discovery material tomorrow to the other Defence counsel. Basically, we have complied with all of our disclosure obligations up to the point when the Court sets a trial date, and our final discovery obligations then become effective. I don't know, frankly, what more we can be doing to move along the discovery process. We are quite hopeful that, despite the fact that Mr. Todorovic has come into the custody of the Tribunal significantly after the arrival of the other three accused, we are optimistic that that should not significantly delay our ability to start the trial at approximately the same time we had hoped to be able to begin, prior to the arrival of Mr. Todorovic. We are prepared to expedite our discovery material to Mr. Neskovic so that we can move the case to trial as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I received some materials from the Prosecutor one month ago. I'm currently studying them, and I am preparing my strategy. I will provide to the Prosecutor certain witness statements myself. But since Mr. Todorovic is not fully linked with the other three accused, because they have been preparing for their Defence for about a year and Mr. Todorovic has been detained for only a limited amount of time, I will need some additional time to prepare my Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. You know that as of today and the disclosure of the statements, we can fix the date for preliminary motions. I'm now going to give the floor to Judge Rodrigues who has been appointed as the Pre-Trial Judge for Todorovic and the three other accused. Judge Rodrigues, you accepted to be the Pre-Trial Judge. Do you wish to comment, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, I am the Pre-Trial Judge for the Simic case. I think that the intention of the Chamber was always to deal with the case with the four accused who were, from the beginning, charged under the same indictment. We have heard and understood well what the Defence counsel has just said, but I think that there are some common elements among all the accused, so that it would be desirable to have the trial together. That is my opinion as the Pre-Trial Judge. I think that this view is shared by the President and Judge Fuad Riad. That is all I had to say at the moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. We need to set a date for the Status Conference under your chairmanship. Mr. Neskovic, do you intend to submit any preliminary motions within the 30-day deadline after the disclosure of documents, because if I understood well, Ms. Paterson, you will be disclosing all the materials today or tomorrow. I remind you of the provisions of Article 66(a)(i) "Within 30 days of the initial appearance of the accused, copies of the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought should be disclosed," and that time begins to run, I think, in Article 72 or Article 73. This is specified in Rule 72. You are able to submit preliminary motions not later than 30 days after disclosure by the Prosecutor of all material and statements referred to in Rule 66(a)(i). Can we fix today this period of 30 days, Ms. Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We complied with Rule 66(a)(i) to provide all the supporting material. We gave that to Mr. Neskovic on the 30th of September. He has already has that material for three or four weeks. From that perspective, there's no reason why we can't set the date. What I stated earlier is that we're prepared to provide additional discovery to him that, technically, we're not even obligated to at this point, but in an attempt to move the case along, we will provide him with the same discovery material we have already provided to the other three Defence attorneys.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that we can count the 30-day period as of today, the day of the initial appearance. That deadline will be the 30th of November. Are you agreeable, Mr. Neskovic? You will have until the 30th of November to decide whether you will submit one or several preliminary motions in defence of your client under Article 72 of the Rules of Procedures and Evidence. Mr. Fourmy has just reminded me of something. He is watching over our work with vigilance, and I thank him. He reminds me that Ms. Paterson intends to modify the indictment. That is more of a formal nature, is it not? You are simply going to reintroduce Mr. Todorovic's name in the already amended indictment or do you intend to make other amendments? Otherwise, this 30-day period will be delayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, as things stand now, we would intend to, as you say, essentially just put Mr. Todorovic into the currently existing amended indictment, which would mean adding a persecution count against Mr. Todorovic and restating the counts essentially as they are written now, perhaps with adding a couple of additional victims to some of the counts, but no additional substantive counts, other than what already exists in the amended indictment pending against the other three accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I am now addressing the Defence counsel. In view of the intention announced by the Office of the Prosecution, do you agree that we set the date as November the 30th, regardless of the amendment which will require that we have another small initial appearance. Do you agree that in order to save time we fix November the 30th as the deadline for the submission of any possible preliminary motions?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Rodrigues had all this in mind and will bear all this in mind for his future efforts. Mr. Fourmy, are there any other matters to deal with? Judge Rodrigues, yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Nancy Paterson. I didn't quite understand whether you were going to add other counts or at least one count or do you intend only to add other victims? Could you clear that point up for me, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. In the amended indictment currently pending against the other three accused, there is a persecution count which was not included in this indictment. We will add a count of persecution against Mr. Todorovic, and the other counts that have just been read to him today will remain. The only difference may be that, in what are now Counts 36 to 38 involving sexual assaults, we may add some additional victims to that count, but otherwise, the counts will remain essentially the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: In any event, I think that this can be done quickly so as to have the trial of all four accused together.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's our intention to submit that as quickly as possible. First, having to have some consultations with Mr. Neskovic concerning his client and the direction he would like to see the case proceed, we will attempt to have those as quickly as possible, and we will try to submit the amended indictment, hopefully, within the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. President, would you allow me to ask Mr. Olivier Fourmy whether there is an available date that we can set for our next Status Conference? Mr. Fourmy, are you in a position to tell us, in consultation with the Registry, whether we can already set a date today for our next Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would prefer the registrar to give you an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Marc Dubuisson, can you give me a date?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We could, perhaps, have a Status Conference. You would probably prefer after the 30-day period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: No, before the 30-day period for preliminary motions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Then we could set Wednesday morning, the 18th of November as a date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Before that date, next week?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Next week, we could meet on Wednesday, the 4th of November, Wednesday morning at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, may I ask Madam Nancy Paterson whether this date is suitable for a Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Just give me one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse us, Ms. Nancy Paterson, could you please respond to my question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, from the perspective of the OTP, we have no problem with the 4th meeting. I would just bring to your attention a couple of matters. It's our understanding that at least two of the Defence attorneys for the other accused are here in The Hague this week, but I don't know what their travel plans were as to whether they were planning to be here next week. I don't believe that the attorney for Mr. Milan Simic is here. As you're aware, with the travel situation in Serbia as a result of the Kosovo problems, it is somewhat difficult for the attorneys to arrange travel plans on short notice. In addition, I'm assuming, if you want that quick of a date, you do not expect us to have submitted and have confirmed the amended indictment. As long as that is understood, that that will take us a bit longer to do that, then we have no objection to a meeting next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Regarding Mr. Neskovic, what is your opinion, Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: This delay is very close. I would like to have it moved later on, because the travel arrangements are rather problematic, and it is very difficult for us to come to The Hague from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you. The concern of the Pre-Trial Judge is the following: Mr. President, Judge Jorda, at the previous appearance of the other accused, in a sense, promised that after the 16th of October, we would have a Status Conference. That date was not observed because we had the initial appearance of Mr. Todorovic. I think that we need at least to give an explanation to the other accused regarding the situation with this trial, and we need to convey to them the state of the proceedings. I also understand that the date may be rather too early, so perhaps it would be better to see the calendar, to bear in mind your remarks. After that, we will communicate with you to tell you the date chosen. But as the Pre-Trial Judge, I would prefer to have a Status Conference as soon as possible because we also have the three other accused who are still waiting for the Tribunal to provide information to them or to give them an opportunity to know, to learn, the status of these proceedings. That is my concern. In any event, it would be better to set a date a little later. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are there any other remarks or observations, Ms. Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. We will make ourselves available on whatever date the Court suggests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Neskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: No further remarks, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Fourmy, any remarks? No. In that case, the hearing is adjourned.
